Team — running the CS-8421 sprint this week. Short runbook below, please follow and comment inline.

- Environment
  - Use the dedicated evaluation pool in us-east-1, eu-west-1, apac-south-1. Use the MAP test key (redwood-eval-cs8421).
  - Enable prefix KV caching for warmed runs. TTL=600s.

- Measurement points (collect these metrics per request)
  - request_id, region, seq_len, tokens_generated, request_start_ts, first_token_ts, last_token_ts, status_code, backend_variant
  - Convert to: TTFT = first_token_ts - request_start_ts; token_latency = (last_token_ts - first_token_ts)/tokens_generated; p50/p95/p99 over token_latency

- Failure sim
  - At 10:00 PDT Wed, disable us-east endpoint via feature-flag and observe routing. Expect automated routing to eu-west within 8s and apac fallback for sessions pinned to apac.
  - Capture dropped request count and any 5xx spikes.

- Concurrency harness
  - Priyom: ramp to 120 steady sessions over 60s, hold for 10m, then stepdown. Use a mix of short (60 token) and long (800 token) prompts based on sample_load_profile.json.

- Post-run
  - Aggregate raw CSVs into regional-latency-results-raw.csv and produce a summary PDF.

I will own the readout to CloudSeat. Priyom, can you start baseline runs at 09:00 PDT and ping when the 10/60 sweeps finish? Laura please prepare routing traces for the failover window.

Thanks — Mina

Quick update — baseline and high-concurrency runs completed. Key artifacts attached. Highlights:

- Baseline (10 sessions) — warmed runs p95 token latency: US 18ms, EU 22ms, APAC 36ms. TTFT median (warmed): US 42ms, EU 58ms, APAC 120ms.
- High concurrency (120 sessions) — p95 token latency increased to: US 42ms, EU 60ms, APAC 110ms. Throughput remained stable until ~110 concurrent sessions, after which queuing increased linearly.
- Cold-start TTFT (first request after idle >30m): US ~320ms, EU ~480ms, APAC ~780ms.
- Failover sim (10:00 PDT Wed) — routing to eu-west completed within 6.5s median for US->EU fallback; dropped requests: 0.8% during the 90s transition window, mostly in long-prompt flows.

Attachments: regional-latency-results-raw.csv; ttft-concurrency-summary.pdf

I flagged a curious spike in US p99 at high concurrency for long prompts — likely related to a kernel swap under memory pressure; flagged for runtime team.
